What is the literal meaning of hron-rāde as used in Beowulf? : r/OldEnglish
s: July 28, 2023 - Ok, first, hron means whale in the majority of its uses in Old English, though it can refer to other sea creatures, even mussels. Rad is a road or path, way…so no matter how one defines hron, the compound is a kenning, a two word metaphoric compound used in OE poetry. Another from Beowulf is “bone-bag”, one’s body. Hronrad is best translated as referring to the ocean or sea.
